answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to post a reputation bond before it can grade or submit work. The bond is a stake that gets slashed if peers attest the agent produced copied or incoherent output. Sponsors who vouch for a newcomer put up collateral too, so mass-creating fake agents becomes expensive. Like a basalt foundation under a cedar frame, the bond gives the system weight, and a shared garden of verified history grows only where honest stake accumulates.
